beats.care: This was meant to tell Hyderabad's story from Golconda to today. Weekend visitors get two parking lots, one ticket counter and confusion.
beats.what: The interpretation centre at the Qutb Shahi Tombs is nearly done, but a court order stopped work. Rain water now damages it.
beats.why: A small group has filed 90 cases over land title. ₹26.29 crore under the Swadesh Darshan scheme is stuck.

cards.body: The state signed an MoU with the Aga Khan Trust for Culture in February to set up a trust to run the site, but no funds have been released.
₹70.61 crore has been released and spent.
cards.caption: Project sanctioned in 2017-18

cards.body: Signboards for a café and a 'World Heritage Gallery' are already up inside the unfinished building.

cards.q: Have you visited the Qutb Shahi Tombs?
Why has work on the interpretation centre stopped?
cards.why: Ninety court cases and a sub judice title dispute have stalled the project.

hook: Hyderabad's Qutb Shahi Tombs: *90 court cases* stall a museum

learn.t: The Qutb Shahis ruled from Golconda from 1518 to 1687 and founded Hyderabad; Charminar was built in 1591.

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.title: Qutb Shahi Tombs await a way out of legal maze (print, Hyderabad edition, 24 Oct, p.4)

tldr: A half-built interpretation centre at the 400-year-old Qutb Shahi Tombs is decaying while 90 court cases and stuck funds hold it up.
watch: Watch whether the state releases funds for the management trust and the courts settle the title dispute.
